audit_notes: Model: same steady 1D roof conduction with linearised sol-air boundary as the other roof coatings. Checks: clean SR 0.90 for 8 rows of closed glass cells with sub-micron BaSO4 under a 40 um transparent glaze is plausible (white glazes alone reach ~0.80; the scattering rows add diffuse reflectance, the glaze adds ~4 % specular and absorbs slightly in the NIR if it contains iron; low-iron frit required). Aged loss 0.04 is a vertical-tile value; horizontal roofs collect more dust and bird droppings, so I set a life-mean loss of 0.05 (aged SR 0.85). Emittance 0.93 for a silicate glaze is consistent with measured glazes (0.90-0.94). Hand result: q = 0.5*(0.15*300 + 150 - 0.93*85)/15.5 = 3.74 W/m2 vs 5.56 W/m2 for the aged acrylic baseline: -33 %. Structural: glaze-on-cellular-glass requires matched expansion (borosilicate ~3.3e-6 1/K for both) to avoid crazing; fired panels on fibre-cement or ceramic substrates; brittle against hail (> 25 mm hail can crack thin skins), so panel thickness >= 8 mm for roofs. Only factory-made panels, not a retrofit paint. Simulation coefficient: U_eff = 0.484 W/m2K.
